extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, PTAB litigants, and counsel handling AIA (PTAB) proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and apply the USPTO final rule governing requests for Director Review of decisions in AIA proceedings (IPR/PGR/derivation), including what decisions are reviewable, timing, format, evidentiary limits, appeal effects, and Director authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions subject to Director Review
rubrics_metrics.description: A party to an AIA proceeding may request Director Review in that proceeding of any: Decision on institution; Final Decision (defined as a final written decision in an IPR or PGR proceeding or a final decision in a derivation proceeding); Decision granting rehearing of a decision on institution or a final decision; Other decision concluding an AIA proceeding (e.g., a termination due to a grant of adverse judgment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original page enumerates each category of decision that may be the subject of a Director Review request; 'Final Decision' is explicitly defined to include final written decisions in IPRs/PGRs and final decisions in derivation proceedings. The 'other decision concluding an AIA proceeding' category includes examples such as termination due to a grant of adverse judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director sua sponte review authority and delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may grant review of the same decisions sua sponte within 21 days after the expiration of the period for filing a request for rehearing, absent exceptional circumstances. Further, the Director may delegate review of a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule formalizes the Director's ability to initiate review on the Director's own motion within a 21-day window after the rehearing-request period expires, but notes an exception for 'exceptional circumstances.' It also permits the Director to delegate review authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing a request for Director Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must be filed within the time period set forth in § 42.71(d) unless an extension is granted by the Director upon a showing of good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests outside the § 42.71(d) period require Director-granted extensions, which demand a showing of good cause. Practitioners should consult § 42.71(d) for the precise filing window applicable to the proceeding type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and length requirements for the request
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must comply with the format requirements of § 42.6(a) and is limited to 15 pages as provided in § 42.24(a)(1)(v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests that do not meet the § 42.6(a) formatting rules or exceed the 15-page limit per § 42.24(a)(1)(v) risk being noncompliant; absent Director authorization, the page limit applies. Practitioners should prepare concise filings that conform to the cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary restrictions on Director Review requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent Director authorization, no new evidence is permitted in a request for Director Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule bars submission of new evidence with the Director Review request unless the Director explicitly authorizes it. Parties should rely on the existing record or seek Director permission before attempting to introduce additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of a Director Review request on appeal timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically, a request for Director Review or the initiation of review does not stay deadlines for parties in the underlying proceeding. But a request for Director Review of a final decision, a decision granting rehearing of a final decision, or any other appealable decision concluding a proceeding will reset the time for appeal until all issues on Director Review are resolved. Director Review decisions on decisions on institution are not appealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should not assume that filing for Director Review will toll appeal deadlines unless the request concerns a final or otherwise appealable decision concluding the proceeding; promotion of appeal timing (reset) applies only for those appealable decisions. Decisions on institution, even when subject to Director Review, are not appealable from the Director Review decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical takeaway and effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule codifies the scope of Director Review and formalizes many of the same interim USPTO procedures already in place post-Arthrex; the final rule goes into effect on October 31, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule is intended to promote 'accuracy, consistency, and integrity of PTAB decision-making in AIA proceedings.' Parties should consider Director Review where applicable starting on the effective date and account for the formalized procedures in litigation planning.
